reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a crucial element – a cross-training session – which is vital for building aerobic fitness without the high impact of trail running. Plan B’s consistent easy runs, while gentle, lack this varied stimulus and the introduction of low-impact cross-training. Furthermore, Plan A includes a longer, slightly more challenging run (60 minutes) that directly addresses building aerobic capacity, something absent in Plan B. While both plans prioritize recovery, Plan A’s structured approach to building a foundation is more strategically aligned with the goal of increasing speed.
